newsitem.title: JAPAN: Traders see no sign of BOJ intervention on dlr.
newsitem.headline: Traders see no sign of BOJ intervention on dlr.

text.p: Traders reacted sceptically to reports that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) had intervened to stop the dollar's sharp rise against the yen on Friday and none of the major Tokyo banks contacted by Reuters said they had handled any yen purchases on behalf of the central bank.
But the reports were enough to help take the dollar off its highs after it hit 120.20 yen, the highest in 47 months.
Some dealers said there may have been some small-scale purchasing but could find no hard evidence to confirm it.
"I think it (the talk) is nothing more than verbal intervention by the government, which is concerned about the yen's rapid fall," a major Japanese bank's chief trader said.
Traders said the BOJ had been in contact with banks to enquire about market direction, a common technique central banks use when they want to signal their displeasure with a market trend.
